lawyer:
Mr. Mohammad Ali, Advocate ------ For the petitioners
Mr. Swapan Kumar Das, A.A.G ------ For the opposite parties
parties:
Md. Nachir Uddin and others
Vs.
Deputy Commissioner, Tangail and other
full_judgment:
Md. Rais Uddin, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 18.9.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Tangail in Title Appeal No.22 of 2006 dismissed the appeal and affirmed those dated 23.2.2006 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Madhupur, Tangail in O.C. Suit No.111 of 2002 dismissed the suit, should not be set-aside.

2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted a suit praying for permanent injunction contending, inter-alia, that the original owner of suit land was Ananta Baishnabi, Kedernath Karmakar and Loknath Karmakar who sold the suit land to Join Uddin Q Joinal Abedin and handedover the possession of the suit land to Joyenuddin and thereafter several transfers were made through kabala deeds and ultimately the predecessors of plaintiff No.1-3 Nurul Islam became the owner of the suit land who died leaving behind plaintiff Nos.1-3 as his heirs. One Mokter Hossain became the owner of the 9 decimals of suit land died leaving behind plaintiff No.4-8 as his heirs and thereby the plaintiffs filed the suit praying for permanent injunction against the defendants who are given threat to disposes the present petitioners from the suit land wherein the present petitioners have been possessing the suit land by constructing dwelling but and living there in and some houses have been possessing by giving rent to the tenants.

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing joint written statements denying material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit land was acquired by the Road and High ways in the year 1940 and it was published in Gazette and prepared L.A. map. The suit land had no possession, right, title of any others except the Road and High ways. The defendants further slated that no notice was served upon the plaintiffs for demolitions their establishment and on 2.11.2002 there was announcement through mike from the authority of Road and High ways to demolish of illegal establishment from the Government land.

4. At the trial the plaintiffs examined 6(six) witnesses and the defendants examined 2(two) witnesses in support of their respective cases.

5. On conclusion of trial the learned Judge of the trial court after hearing the parties and considering evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 23.02.2006. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred appeal before the learned District Judge, Tangail. On transfer it was heard and disposed of by the teamed Additional District Judge, 2nd Court who after hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court by his judgment and decree dated 18.09.2008.

6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree the plaintiffs as petitioners moved this court and obtained the instant Rule.

7. Mr. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed the Revisional Application, pleadings, evidence, judgment and decree of the courts below and other materials on record before this court and submits that the trial court failed to discuss the evidence of the plaintiffs and the defendants, moreover in his finding found the possession of the plaintiffs. He submits that the appellate court on discussion of the evidence both oral and documentary in his finding found the possession and prima facie title of the plaintiffs but dismissed the appeal on misconception of law, fact and circumstances of the case on the ground that the suit land is not specified by mentioning boundary in the schedule of the plaint which is not sustainable in law. He lastly submits that finding and observation of the courts below are not based on evidence and materials on record and as such judgment and decree of the courts below are not sustainable in law and he prayed for to make the rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the courts below.

8. In support of his contention he has referred the decisions, reported in: (1) 8 BLC (AD) 72, (2) 16 BLC 727, (3) I1 BLT (AD) 124, (3) 56 DLR (AD) 22.

9. Mr. Swapan Kumar Das, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the Opposite-parties opposed the rule and submits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title by producing original deed. He submits that in the Suit there are 8 plaintiffs with separate holding has not been mentioned in the plaint. He submits that plaintiffs filed S.A. Khatian but failed to submit any deed in support of their, Khatian which is not acceptable and sustainable in law. He submits that in the plaint there is no specification of the boundary under Order VII rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that the plaintiffs failed to make any statement in the plaint about the original via deed. He lastly submits that concurrent finding of facts reached by the courts below and there is no misreading and non-consideration of the evidence and as such there is no reason to interfere by this court in revision and he prayed for discharged the rule.

10. In support of his contention, he has referred the decisions reported in: (1)21 BLD 163, (2) 12 BLC (AD) 36, (3) 64 DLR (AD) 133.

11. In order to appreciate the submission made by the learned advocates for the parties, I have gone through the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits, judgment and decree of the courts below and the relevant provision of law very carefully.

12. Now the question calls for consideration whether the learned Judge of the courts below has committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decisions occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree.

13. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiffs brought the suit for permanent injunction against the defendants. The plaintiffs claimed the suit land by purchase.

14. In support of their claimed submitted two deeds marked as exhibit-4 and 4Ka, Khatian exhibit-I, Trade license exhibit-2, 2Ka, electric bills, rent receipts, holding taxes, receipt of Pour taxes marked as exhibit-3 series, Mutation Purcha exhibit-5, Dakhila exhibit-5Ka, electricity bill of the houses marked as exhibit-9 series, Mutation Khatian of Khatian No.822 exhibit-10.

15. The learned Judge of the trial court considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit with the finding-

“বাদীদের পূর্ববর্তীদের নামে নালিশী জমি বাবদ এস, এ খতিয়ান প্রদঃ ১(খ) প্রস্তুত হওয়া দ্বারা নালিশী জমিতে বাদীদের পূর্ববর্তীর স্বত্ব ছিল এটা প্রতিষ্ঠিত বা প্রমানিত হয় না কারণ খতিয়ান দ্বারা কোন জমিতে খতিয়ান প্রস্তুত কালে খতিয়ানে উল্লেখিত ব্যক্তি দখলে ছিলেন (পৃষ্ঠ নং-৯) এটাই প্রমানিত হয়। বাদীপক্ষ নালিশী জমিতে দখলে থাকার সমর্থনে খাজনার দাখিলা প্রদঃ ৫ সিরিজ হিসেবে দালিলিক সাক্ষ্যরূপে দাখিল করেছে এবং পি,ডব্লিউ-২ থেকে পি-ডব্লিউ-৬ পর্যন্ত সকল মৌখিক সাক্ষ্যরা নালিশী জমিতে বাদী পক্ষের দখলে থাকার স্বপক্ষে পরস্পরকে সমর্থন করে সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেছে এবং বিবাদীপক্ষের সাক্ষী পি-ডব্লিউ ১ ও তার দেয় সাক্ষ্যের জেরায় স্বীকার করে যে, নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষ দখলে আছে। তবে যেহেতু বাদী পক্ষ নালিশী জমিতে তাদের আপাতঃ স্বত্ব (prima facie titel) এর দাবী প্রমানে ব্যর্থ হয়েছে সেহেতু নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষের দখল আইন কর্তৃক সমর্থিত দখল নয়।”

16. It further appears that the learned Judge of the appellate court considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court with the finding-

“ইহা স্বীকৃত যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তি সি,এস ৪৪ ও ৪৫ খতিয়ানভূক্ত। উক্ত সম্পত্তি সি,এস রেকর্ডীয় মালিকদের ওয়ারিশগন বাদীগনের পূর্ববর্তীদের নিকট বিক্রয় করেন মর্মে দাখিলী কাগজাদী হতে পরিলক্ষিত হয় এবং তাদের ওয়ারিশদের নামে এস,এ ১০০ খতিয়ানে রেকর্ড হয় মর্মে দেখা যায়। বিবাদীপক্ষ ইহা স্বীকার করেন এবং বাদী ও বাদীগনের পূর্ববর্তীদের নিকট হতে খাজনা আদায় করা হয় ইহাও স্বীকার করেন। ফলে নালিশী সম্পত্তির রেকর্ড সংক্রান্ত বিষয়ে কোন অসামঞ্চস্যতা নাই। কিন্তু বিবাদী পক্ষ দাবী করেন যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তি ১৯৪০ সনে সড়ক ও জনপথের জন্য অধিগ্রহন করা হয়েছে। এই মর্মে গেজেটের অংশ সত্যায়িত দাখিল করেন। কিন্তু দীর্ঘদিনের মধ্যে কেন তাদের নামে অধিগ্রহন কৃত সম্পত্তি রেকর্ড হলো না ইহা আদালতের নিকট বোধগম্য নয়। এখানে উল্লেখ্য বাদীর আরজীর তপশীলে নাঃ সম্পত্তি ১৮ শতক মর্মে দাবী করেন। জবানবন্দী দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় ৮ জন বাদী ৮টি দোকানের মালিক মর্মে উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে। উক্ত দখলকৃত সম্পত্তির পরিমান সুনির্দিষ্টভাবে উল্লেখ করেন নাই। তদুপরি বাকী সম্পত্তি কিভাবে কোথায় আছে সে সম্পর্কে কোন সাক্ষ্য আদালতে উপস্থাপন করে নাই। ফলে নালিশী সম্পত্তি সুনির্দিষ্ট ও সুস্পষ্ট নয় মর্মে প্রতীয়মান হয়। বাদীগনের বায়াদের বিষয়ে যে সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেছেন অর্থাত মালিকানার দলিল সম্পর্কে জাবেদা নকল দিয়েছেন কিন্তু মূল দলিল সম্পর্কে কোন ব্যাখ্যা নাই। ফলে নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বাদীদের স্বত্ব সুস্পষ্ট নয়।”

<u>17. In a suit for permanent injunction the plaintiffs shall have to prove their exclusive possession in the suit land in order to get decree. The court may incidentally enquired into prima facie title of the parties and the court need not enter into disputed title unless the possession of the plaintiffs is clearly established by evidences of the plaintiffs. The courts below have dealt mainly on the point of title of the plaintiffs which should not have been the consideration in a suit for permanent injunction. The findings of the courts as to possession of the suit land on the basis of evidence on record.</u>

18. In the instant case both the courts below concurrently found exclusive possession of the plaintiffs but the trial court observed that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in the suit land. The learned Judge of the appellate court found possession as well as prima facie title of the plaintiffs with the finding-

“উক্ত সম্পত্তি সি,এস রেকর্ডীয় মালিকদের ওয়ারিশগণ বাদীগণের পূর্ববর্তীদের নিকট বিক্রয় করেন মর্মে দাখিলী কাগজাদী হতে পরিলক্ষিত হয় এবং তাদের ওয়ারিশদের নামে এস,এ ১০০ খতিয়ানে রেকর্ড হয় মর্মে দেখা যায়। বিবাদীপক্ষ ইহা স্বীকার করেন এবং বাদী ও বাদীগনের পূর্ববর্তীদের নিকট হতে খাজনা আদায় করা হয় ইহাও স্বীকার করেন। ফলে নালিশী সম্পত্তির রেকর্ড সংক্রান্ত বিষয়ে কোন অসামঞ্জস্যতা নাই।”

19. The learned Judge of the appellate court dismissed the appeal on the ground that the suit land was not specified in the schedule.

20. In this connection I feel it necessary to put the relevant provision of law under Order VII rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the relevant portion of the plaint in the schedule which as under:

21. Order VII rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure-

"Where the subject-matter of the suit is immovable property, the plaint shall contain a description of the property sufficient to identify it, and, in case such property can be identified by boundaries or numbers in a record of settlement of survey, the plaint shall specify such boundaries or numbers."

22. The relevant portion of the plaint in the schedule

তফশিল

জেলা- টাংগাইল, থানা- মধুপুর, মৌজা-মধুপুর।

সেঃমেঃ খং নং	আর,ও,আর খং নং	দাগ নং	শ্রেণী	পরিমান

৪৪	১০০	২০৮	বাড়ী	.১০ শতাংশ

৪৫	“	২০৮/৭০৬	কান্দা	মোট .১৮ শতাংশ

চৌহদ্দি

যাহার উত্তরে- প্রতাপ সিংহ

দক্ষিণে- জোয়াদ ডাঃ এর স্ত্রী

পূর্বে-সি,এন্ড বি রাস্তা

পশ্চিমে- জেলা বোর্ডের রাস্তা

এই চৌহদ্দির মধ্যে .১৮ শতাংশ ভূমি যেখানে বাদীপক্ষের ইউপেটার্নের টিন সেট বিল্ডিং ১টা, এল পেটানের টিন সেট বিল্ডিং ১টা, ল্যাট্রিন ৩টা, ইসলামিয়া গেস্ট হাউজ ১টা একতলা বিশিষ্ট, টিপটপ কনফেকশনারী আশা ফাষ্টফুড এন্ড কনফেকশনারী ১টা বাংলাদেশ বই ঘর ১টা, সেলুন ৩টা, বীজ ভান্ডার ১টা, বলকানাইজিং ও ওয়র্কশপ১টা, হোন্ডা এবং টেম্পুর পার্টের দোকান ২টা, গ্রীল ওয়ার্কশপ ১টা অবস্থিত।

23. From a plain reading of the above quoted portion of the plaint of the schedule and relevant provision of law it is clearly and specifically stated the schedule of the land by giving plots number as well as boundary compliance of the mandatory requirement of law in giving description sufficient to identify the suit land and as such the appellate court on misconception of law and misinterpretation of the schedule of the plaint arrived at the wrong decision which are not sustainable in law.

24. Now, let me see the legal position of the case in the light of decisions cited from the Bar.

25. The decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioners, reported in:

(1) 8 BLC (AD) 72, wherein their lordships held-

"The suit for permanent injunction is essentially a suit for possession. Though the title may be incidentally gone into but in a suit for permanent injunction the Court need not enter into disputed question of title except to the extent as it would help in finding which of the parties have possession. The plaintiff could not bring home their possession in the suit land for a decree for a permanent injunction."

(2) 11 BLT (AD) 124, wherein their lordships held-

"All the Courts below have considered the legality or otherwise of the award by which the plaintiffs claim title to the suit land but without considering the evidence on record as to possession both the trial court and the Court and the Court of appeal below decreed the suit for permanent injunction. The High Court Division as well without considering the evidence as to possession dismissed the suit for permanent injunction. The suit being a suit for permanent injunction in which the question of title may be gone into incidentally but decision of title in a suit for permanent injunction ought not to have been the guiding principle. The Court cannot disentitle the plaintiff of a decree for permanent injunction if he can prove possession and in thin view the plaintiff could not be evicted with force if continues to be in possession unless in due process of law and could exercise his right of possession restraining everybody including the real owners. In a suit for permanent injunction the Court need not enter into disputed title except to the extent that it would help the Court in finding which of the parties have prima facie title and exclusive possession.

26. The decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties, reported in:

(1)21 BLD 163, wherein their lordships held –

"Although the S.A. Khatian stood in the name of Hasina Jamil but the S.A. Khatian cannot confer any title in respect of any landed property to anybody. The learned Judge Found that the suit property as per schedule of the plaint is 1.29 acres of land which appertains to plot No.38 of C.S. Khatian No. 179 but unfortunately, the said property was not found in C.S. Khatian No. 179. The learned Judge also found from Ext. I the sale deed normally registered on 30.3.1939 and he purchased the property of C.S. plot No.28 and not C.S. Plot No.38 of S.A. Khatian No.179. Accordingly the learned Judge dismissed the suit and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court, upon a reading of C.S. Khatian Ext. 3(a) not Ext. 3 as the learned Judge referred the C.S. Khatian No.179 and the hal khatian No. 422, dag As stated as 38 but quantity of land measured 1.29 acres of land was sold. The learned Judge termed the discrepancy as simple anomaly."

(2)12 BLC (AD) 36, wherein their lordships held —

"Plaintiff for the purpose of success in his suit and thereupon to have the relief sought in the suit is required first, to establish that the suit as framed is maintainable and that when the Court finds that the suit is maintainable then goes for consideration of the claim of the plaintiffs in respect of the subject matter of the suit and that while the claim made in the suit is being established by legal evidence, the Court passes a decree in favour of the plaintiff and if it is otherwise then dismisses the suit. Thus, the plaintiff is to establish first for having the relief in the suit instituted by him that his suit as framed is maintainable and if same is not established then generally the Court is not required to go for adjudication of other contentions making which relief has been sought in the suit"

(3) 64 DLR (AD) 133, wherein their lordships held-

"When a finding of fact is based on consideration of the materials on record, those findings are immuned from interference by the revisional Court except there is non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence on record. The High Court Division has no jurisdiction to sit on appeal over a finding of fact. It is concerned with the questions as to whether the appellate court in giving a particular finding has committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice as such finding is found to have resulted from glaring misconception of law or there is misreading or non-consideration of material evidence in arriving at such finding."

27. The law 'is now Well settled that the finding of facts, whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate court is binding on High Court Division, as a revisional court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances, such as non, consideration or misreading of the material evidence and misinterpretation of law which affect the merit of the case.

28. In the instant case both the courts below found the possession of the plaintiffs and the appellate court also found the prima facie title of the plaintiffs but dismissed the appeal on the ground that the suit land is not specified in the boundary which is misinterpretation and misconception of law as stated above. The plaintiffs having complied with the mandatory requirement of law in giving description by numbers and boundaries is quite identifiable and not vague and as such suit property can be identified by boundaries and numbers. The appellate court on misconception of law and misinterpretation of the schedule of the plaint arrived at the wrong decision which are not sustainable.

29. In view of the discussions, decisions and reasons stated above, I am lead to hold that the judgment and decree passed by the courts below cannot be sustained in law and are liable to be set aside. Thus, 1 find merit in the rule.

30. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree of the courts below are set aside and the suit is decreed.

31. There will be no order as to costs. The order of status-quo granted earlier by this court stand vacated.

32. Let the Lower Court Record along with the judgment and decree be sent to the court below at once.

End.
